title: Direct negative space with a measurable brief
goal: Use object size and position as composition requirements rather than vague adjectives.
explanation: “Minimalist” can describe style without specifying layout. Define the main object, its approximate image area and where empty space belongs. The goal is not a mathematically exact segmentation model: use a rough grid and disclose estimation limits. A usable composition still needs visual hierarchy and an intentional subject.
sampleInput: Scene: one plain coffee mug on an off-white background. Mug in the lower-right region; approximately 5–10% of frame area. Keep the upper-left two-thirds open for a future title, but do not generate any text or logo.
prompt: Create one original minimal flat-lay image with a single plain mug in the lower-right. Use soft daylight and a solid warm off-white background. The mug should occupy roughly 5–10% of the full image area. Keep the upper-left two-thirds visually empty. No text, logos, extra props or dramatic texture.
workedExample: Overlaying a simple 10×10 grid helps estimate occupied area. A mug spanning about 2×3 cells has a bounding area around 6%, though its actual silhouette is smaller. A large shadow or extra spoon may interfere with the intended title space.

steps.title: Specify the layout
steps.text: Write size, position and empty-region requirements before generating.

steps.title: Create one image
steps.text: Keep the original prompt/settings and the unedited output.

steps.title: Estimate with a grid
steps.text: Approximate the object’s bounding area and note shadow/shape limitations.

steps.title: Test the empty region
steps.text: Place a temporary text box in a separate editor to see whether the intended title area is usable.

steps.title: Refine the weakest condition
steps.text: Adjust scale or positioning language once, retaining both versions for comparison.

checks: The output contains exactly one mug and no text or unwanted props.
The area estimate and its bounding-box limitation are documented.
The upper-left title region is demonstrably usable, not merely described as minimalist.
commonMistakes: Treating “minimalist” as a precise placement instruction.
Claiming exact object-area measurement from a rough visual estimate.
offline: Draw the scene on a 10×10 grid and reserve the title region before choosing the mug size.
reflection: Did the shadow consume more useful space than the mug itself?

evidence.title: Keep the build
evidence.detail: Save your original input, exact prompt and resulting artifact. The output contains exactly one mug and no text or unwanted props.

evidence.title: Show what you tested
evidence.detail: Record a pass/fail result and evidence for every check below. The area estimate and its bounding-box limitation are documented.

evidence.title: Explain a limitation
evidence.detail: Write what changed after one deliberate revision and name a remaining failure mode. Treating “minimalist” as a precise placement instruction.
